html:
The River

Halliwell is the father of all rivers. The twelve rivers of the North and East flow into the Smokey Dahl, and only one flows from it, carrying the waters south into the ocean: the sacred Holliwell. (Smoky Distance) The Polari Lands Guide calls it the greatest river of the entire continent. Its delta lies at the town of Surlion, with one foot in Litland, the other in the kingdom of Shimmery; a huge delta pervades and moistens Litland. (Litland) The sacred river feeds its waters Shepherds Luga and Almera. In the spring, Holliwell spills for a mile, flooding the islands and rapids; at this time, as Minerva Moranu said, only two crossings remain: the Cool Threshold at the border fortress in Litland and the Julian Bridge. There are barges along Halliwell: the prophet Francis-Ilianus floated along it, getting to Darkwater. (Francis-Ilian)

The Julian Bridge is an arched giant mile long, a "miracle of Yangmei architecture". It was erected by the sovereign Julian the Great, and he connected West Almera with Holliwell County, conquering the river for the first time, "a hitherto unruly architect." Over the bridge, the Shavans were able to sell cattle to the central lands at any time of the year, and, according to the Shadow of the Great Tree, "a whole rain of silver" poured on the Steppe; it was for the bridge, and not for the laws, that the Shavans fell in love with Juliana. At the western end of the bridge stands Fort Glorious Watch, the most western outpost of the Crown, built to keep the shanties of different counties from fighting at the entrance to the bridge. Nearby, at the fork of the tracks to Rei-Roy, Corden and Fais, stands the wooden town of Trident.

Stupid War

According to the Guide, in the early 18th century, the Dukes of Almer sent mechanics to Halliwell to assess the possibility of building a dam for a spark shop. Halliwell's Shavans were enraged to block the sacred river with a wall! - declared war on Almera, attacked her western lands for six months, captured Clermie and held Blackmore under siege. The mechanics under the protection of the knights finished the measurements and came to the conclusion that a spark shop on Holliwell is impossible: the river is too powerful. The war was called Stupid, and the expression "to fight for the dam" became a saying - to defend what is not worth the eaten egg.

Frontier of the West

Halliwell separates the Great Steppe from the central lands. On both banks are the Shepherd's Meadows, a fertile steppe about a hundred miles wide and four hundred miles long, similar to the "grass sea", where one mile is no different from the other. Nomads have long fought for them with Almera, Hope and Litland. In the sixteenth century, after the Horse Wars, Juliana declared the Meadows a shared possession: three western counties and three eastern lands received the right to graze cattle on both banks. In the lower course of the river there are four fords, along which nomads distill herds. Litland fortresses on these fords look after the crossings; each ford has its own fortress, and two pigeons are sent there. Rebecca Litland grew up in such a fortress among the Shepherd's Meadows.

Holliwell County

Geography

One of the free counties of the West is named after the river. According to the Guide, it lies in the Midwest, between the Sunset Coast to the north, the Race to the south, the Mills, and the Shepherd's Meadows with Smoke Dahlia on the other side. (Reis (County)) This is a plain where the fertile part along the Smoky Distance and Shepherd's Meadows and the steppe part, closer to the Mills, are clearly distinguished. The proximity of the lake and the great river makes the eastern Holliwell very fertile. The county capital is Corden; the trade route from Julianine Bridge to Corden was paved by Halliwell's chavans, who wished to gain a share in the cattle trade following Reis.

The steppe part lies in the west, closer to the Mills, fertile - in the east, at the Smoky Distance.

Economy

According to the Guide, the county's economy is mixed: west Holliwell is pastoral and similar to Reis, and there are irrigated arable land in the east, along the Smoky Distance. The local horses are known: Harmon, not being an expert, still knew that the “holiwell” is distinguished from the Lithuanian or the Fowley.

People and Customs

The inhabitants of the county - the hillmen (in the novels they are called "halls") - have much in common with rheas: freedom, semi-nomadic life, the struggle for the herds and the worship of the forces of nature. But the river changes a lot. Fertile lands require protection, so there are more settled people, there are cities, castles and landowners with their wives, feudal and vassal ties are stronger. A special type of fortifications - "land belts": low, but very long, up to tens of miles, ramparts with palisades and moats that protect arable land from nomads and at the same time serve as irrigation channels. The lords of East Halliwell rarely fight themselves, but often by the hands of the Western Shavans under their control. Hall was also Niza: she was born in Halliwell, and Ganta Thunderstorm took her prisoner and sold her into slavery; another native of the county, Catherine Catherine, was sold to the south and became an altess of Prince Hector.

If the reins deify movement and space, then the hills are water: a person came out of the water and will return to it after death. In Smoky Distance and Halliwell, according to their legends, live myrids (underwater witches), mermaids, lake fairies, berets with heads of pike and marosins - spirits of currents and whirlpools, and rules the water world Drop-God, whose body consists of all the water of the river and lake. Although the hills have long seen the Ocean of the Abyss, the home of the Drops-God is still considered a lake: the ocean is “too huge.” Near Korden under the waters of the Smoky Distance is the Cathedral of Water Deities, from which through hundreds of mica windows you can see the bottom of the lake with stone idols and the bones of sacrificial animals. The Shadow of the Great Tree says that one of the three roots of the First Tree of the Pramatery was planted "in the western part of the Smoky Distance, off the coast of Holliwell County."

The historical enemies of the hillen are the rei: the hillen despise them for wildness and worship of the horned beast, the rei of the hillens for digging in the soil "like worms"; many songs of both lands consist of mocking each other. In 1775, when the horde passed by the Trident, the halls were accused of robbing reys.

Ruling House

According to the Guide, the Earls of Holliwell have some real power - unlike the Earls of Reis - thanks to the trade routes through the Smokey Dale and the river fleet on Holliwell: Shavans who want to sell cattle, meat and skin are forced to bow to them. But in war, the Shavans obey not the count, but the most experienced gauntlet. The arbitrariness of the local counts is also familiar to merchants: Victor Shayland's great-grandfather and his whole family fled from Halliwell, when the local count decided that he had the right to take money from merchants for the sake of maintaining the army. (Vittor Shayland) In "Only One Star" there is a letter according to which Count Halliwell hands over to his two knights one-guarded villages on the edge of the Shepherd's Meadows; Mark, who investigated her disappearance, considered Halliwell one of the wildest lands of the Empire, where small knights are little different from robbers and can not read.

History

According to the Guide, Halliwell was settled simultaneously from two sides: from the east by farmers from Almera, from the west by nomadic tribes from Reis, and from the 7th to the 10th centuries passed in their irreconcilable enmity. In the tenth century, the Kreydor family began selling the Shavans good, cheap steel, crossbows, and mail, asking only that they plunder whoever the Kreydors named; by pitting the Shavans against one another and making them dependent on their weapons, the Kreydors had subjugated most of the lands by the twelfth century, adopted the sacred river’s name, Hollywell, and applied it to the entire region, which had not previously even been united. In confirmation of the right to the sacred name, they erected the Cathedral of Water Deities. In the twelfth century, a substantial part of Hollywell was absorbed by the Empire of the Iron Sun, and the wars against the Mills, according to the “Guide”, “were neither foolish nor small”; for centuries, they remained a struggle for survival for the Shavans. In the First Horse War, Rays and Holliwell's Shavans under Darian the Bad trampled Almera, Hope, and Litland.

In the Events of the Series

The Holliwell Rail Road was built under Telurian. Control of the four lower fords became a stake in the intrigues around the 1774 fair of brides: Erwin Origin proposed to the Litlands to get the fords into a lazy possession, although this was contrary to Julian's law, and Reis' ambassadors accused Adrian of having given the sacred crossings to the Litlands by letter; Adrian himself considered this lazy letter a forgery planted for the sake of provok. (Adrian) After the assassination of Count Damir Reis, the Shavans took possession of the crossings, and the Moran horde invaded Litland; Holliwell's "wind-horsemen" fought in it - thousands of county warriors joined the campaign. In the spring of 1775, Minerva, demanding that Moran take the horde for Holliwell, threatened that on the rails and across the Julian Bridge, a regiment of spark cavalry would occupy the Cool Threshold in a week, and then the Shavans, whose families and herds remained in the west, would not be able to return home until the water fell. After being sworn in, Minerva promised that the Luga Shepherds would remain common under Julian law and the Litlands would no longer attempt to appropriate them; the condition was that the Shavans would become loyal vassals and would never again pass Holliwell. In the pigeon cage she had two birds: with an order to General Silver Fox NOT to occupy the Cool Threshold and with a request to the Duke of Origin NOT to send troops to the West; if the ambassadors of the Crown were killed, the birds would not fly away.

In the summer of that year, Paul and Alanis crossed the river below Beck's confluence, bound for Rei-Roy. Soon, Erwin's fleet moved down Holliwell from Smoky Distance - the cairns poured onto the deck as the ships passed under Julian Bridge. The ships docked at Mayhor, at the ferry crossing, from where Erwin rode lightly to Rei-Roy, and the abandoned ships on the first night burned the gant Ondei, who sought Erwin along the banks of the river. Paul, taking the Glorious Watch and defeating the corps of the Snow Count Lilliday, invited the captive northerners to flee to Holliwell under the shots of their riflemen, and then the horde crossed the Julian bridge and broke into the Red Land. The remnants of Erwin's detachment, having learned of the fall of the Glorious Watch, left the river to the west, to the Mills.

In the House of 1775, Holliwell's representatives, along with Reis, supported Maurice Labelin's displeasure with the bidding for the Shimmerian eyes, and then condemned his daughter's diversion; the western edge of the hall made it possible for Halliwell to join in the issue of approval of Origin's actions. General Oris, who held the capital of the Sunset Coast, reached agreement with Halliwell's Shavans.

In "Fantasies"

In Fantasies, which the author calls possible futures, Halliwell is mentioned as follows:

  • "Closer - Further" (August 1776). Before returning to Rei-Roy, Ganta Court visited Holliwell and stole several thousand cattle from there. "The Horde at Holliwell's Shore" disturbs the Church seeking peace between the Origin and the Steppe. In the election of Lord Steppe, there are four votes: two from Reis and two from Holliwell.
  • "Ad-ri-an!" (Election 1776). Adrian secretly promised the Shavans of Halliwell County to the Main and the Valley of the Twins from the division of the lands of Origin, and Halliwell was listed among the seven votes in his favor. During the siege of the House, Origin's supporters from the west coast behind a barrel of Laem wine dreamed of paving the rail path from Laham to Waymar across all the lands of the West, fed by a giant spark dam on Holliwell built with the help of the Gauntlet of Power, the very thing that was once recognized as impossible by the mechanics of the Stupid War.

Trivia

  • In The Shadows of the Great Tree, Shavans distinguish their slaves by their origin; one of these possibilities is the "daughter of the Holi people from the banks of the Smoky Distance", who is "not shavanka at all".
  • Neymir, boasting combat experience, called among the opponents "the wind-horses of Halliwell."
